source_text:
Μὴ πλανᾶσθε, ἀδελφοί μου: οἱ οἰκοφθόροι βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν.
εἰ οὖν οἱ κατὰ σάρκα ταῦτα πράσσοντες ἀπέθανον, πόσῳ μᾶλλον, ἐὰν πίστιν θεοῦ ἐν κακῇ διδασκαλίᾳ φθείρῃ, ὑπὲρ ἧς Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐσταυρώθη; ὁ τοιοῦτος ῥυπαρὸς γενόμενος, εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἄσβεστον χωρήσει, ὁμοίως καὶ ὁ ἀκούων αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: Warning against corrupters of the faith
orientation: Ignatius is warning the Ephesians about false teachers who corrupt the faith, continuing his argument that believers must live as temples of God.
pass_a_gloss: Do not be deceived, my brothers: the house-destroyers [the] kingdom of God will not inherit. If therefore those according to flesh these things practicing died, how much more, if [someone] [the] faith of God in evil teaching corrupts, on behalf of which Jesus Christ was crucified? Such a one filthy having become, into the fire the unquenchable will go, likewise also the one hearing him.

choices.why: The compound means literally 'destroyers of a house/household'; keeping the compound sense preserves the image of tearing down the church as God's household.

choices.english: will not inherit the kingdom of God
choices.why: The future indicative with οὐ is a strong denial; 'inherit' is the standard rendering of κληρονομέω in this Pauline idiom.
rejected: will not receive as an inheritance

choices.english: those who practice these things according to the flesh
choices.why: κατὰ σάρκα is a fixed Pauline phrase meaning 'according to the flesh'; 'practice' captures the habitual force of the present participle.
rejected: those who do these things in the flesh
those acting carnally in these things

choices.why: The dative with ἐν marks the instrument or sphere of corruption; 'evil teaching' keeps the noun διδασκαλία visible rather than collapsing it into an adjective.
The aorist participle marks a completed state of defilement; 'filthy' preserves the moral uncleanness of ῥυπαρός.

choices.english: the one who listens to him
choices.why: The present participle with genitive object means ongoing attentive listening, not mere hearing; 'listens to' captures the receptive posture Ignatius condemns.

bible_refs.note: οἱ οἰκοφθόροι βασιλείαν θεοῦ οὐ κληρονομήσουσιν echoes Paul's list of wrongdoers who will not inherit the kingdom of God

pass_b_english: Do not be deceived, my brothers: those who destroy households will not inherit the kingdom of God.

If those who practice these things according to the flesh have died, how much more will the one who corrupts the faith of God with evil teaching, the faith for which Jesus Christ was crucified? Such a person, having become filthy, will go into the unquenchable fire, and the one who listens to him will do the same.

last_rejected.why: οἰκοφθόροι means corrupters of a household; in context it refers to those who corrupt the faith, not physical house-destroyers.
last_rejected.ruling: οἰκοφθόροι = house‑destroyers; literal translation matches Greek, metaphorical sense acceptable

polish.changed: Clarified the rhetorical question by removing the repeated clause and making the subject explicit, so the reader can follow who goes into the fire and who shares that fate.

notes.why: Multiple metaphors for heresy (myths, teaching, deceit, pleasure, plants, offshoots) may seem like different threats.
notes.fix: Add marginal note identifying these as varied metaphors for same danger.
